blockingIssues.description: The broker-seeded Linear auth path still reads locally stored secret-backed credentials (and may fall back to the generic Hack auth session) before it can mint a broker-backed token, so repo-bound Linear commands can still hit the blocking macOS keychain path despite reporting `tokenSource: "broker"`.

The web env-management slice discards per-variable classification data and only renders aggregate cards, so users still cannot see whether a specific env key is local plaintext, secret-backed, or portable/shared even though CLI and API now expose that value-level status.

Gateway and daemon route validation still runs on normalized `URL.pathname`, so raw dot-segment traversal requests can collapse into unrelated daemon routes instead of being rejected as malformed before routing.

The outage-mode proof only covers env and tickets paths; it never validates sessions or repo-local project operations even though VAL-CROSS-001 explicitly includes them, so the claimed CLI-optional-by-default regression remains incomplete.

Mission closeout evidence is tied to the generic `latestPublished` status update metadata rather than a closeout-specific artifact, so any later unrelated publish can silently overwrite the closeout trail surfaced in CLI and web views.

nonBlockingIssues.description: When repo-bound env commands fail, the web fallback labels the degraded state as `local_only` instead of surfacing an explicit unknown or unavailable state.
The feature commit also edited an unrelated scrutiny review file from another milestone, which is harmless but makes the feature diff less isolated.

Mutation-source validation still fails open when `hack.env.json` is malformed because parse failures degrade to the default contract, allowing a secret-backed key to bypass the new fail-closed guard in that edge case.
Regression coverage adds encoded-segment and invalid-id cases but still does not exercise raw dot-segment traversal requests on the server side.

appliedUpdates.description: Added reusable env-status commands (`env_list_json`, `env_backend_status_json`, and `env_status_smoke`) to `.factory/services.yaml` so future validators can gather VAL-ENV-001 CLI evidence without ad-hoc shell history.

Updated `.factory/library/environment.md` to document Bun dot-segment URL normalization, the deterministic auth-broker root-env fallback helper, the env trust/custody/portability/shared-state taxonomy, and the `HACK_SECRETS_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN_FALLBACK` knob.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: For Linear auth-path hardening work, explicitly warn that `./dist/hack linear status --json` reporting `tokenSource: "broker"` is not sufficient proof of a keychainless flow; require verification that the broker authorization path itself avoids local secret/keychain reads or capture a stronger negative signal.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `linear-keychainless-credential-path` review found that the worker treated `tokenSource=broker` as proof of success even though `src/control-plane/extensions/linear/auth.ts` still reads local secret-backed state before broker seeding can happen.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Bring the required-skill section in sync with the actual available skill inventory, or document an explicit fallback when helper skills like `hack-cli` and `linear` are not installed in the worker session.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `env-trust-custody-status-surfaces` worker handoff had to mark procedure deviations because the skill required `hack-cli` and `linear`, but those skill IDs were not actually available in the session.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify when `agent-browser` is mandatory for web-visible slices that mainly add fallback state or non-visual seams, and require workers to record a justified deviation when they validate such changes only with unit tests plus CLI/curl proof.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `cli-optionality-and-offline-env-regression` review found a web-visible env fallback seam shipped without any `agent-browser` run, but the current skill language still reads as an unconditional browser-validation requirement for `apps/web` user-flow changes.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Carry forward the mission rule that user-facing web changes owned by control-plane workers still need `agent-browser` validation, rather than allowing curl/text scraping alone to count as complete proof.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `mission-linear-closeout-audit` review found a web-visible closeout surface was validated only with routed-page curl/text output because the current control-plane-worker skill mentions CLI and curl/API checks but not the mission's browser-validation requirement.
